_comment: Golden vectors for the PDF report's presentation arithmetic.
Read by BOTH suites: ReportChartTests (Swift) and ReportChartVectorTest (Kotlin).
labelIndices IS COMPUTED IN 32-BIT FLOAT, and that is not an accident of the
Kotlin source: `((n - 1).toFloat() / (target - 1))` truncates differently from
the same expression in Double for 16 of the first 400 series lengths. n = 32 —
a month of daily buckets — is one of them. Swift therefore uses Float too, and
these vectors would catch it if either side stopped.
Colours must match: the same drinking would otherwise print in different
colours on the two platforms.
abbreviateWeekday pins the UNIT of the two-character weekday cut, added in
the 0.84.0 QA round. Kotlin's String.take(2) counts UTF-16 code units;
Swift's String.prefix(2) counts grapheme clusters. For all 21 shipped
languages the two agree, so nothing visible changed - but the combining-accent
and surrogate-pair cases below are where they part, and they are the reason
the Swift side now spells UTF-16 out instead of taking its default.
'ceiling' pins the 100 % mark of each chart: trendCeiling(tallest, limit)
for the trend chart (cases carrying 'limit'), barCeiling(tallest) for the hour
and weekday charts. Until v0.86.0 Android held the factors as literals in its
builder; both builders now call these.
labelIndices cases may carry 'target' (default 8, the report); the Statistics
screen asks for 6 and reads the same function since v0.86.0.

pct.description: a value against a positive maximum
a zero maximum yields zero rather than a division by zero
a negative maximum is treated as no maximum
a value above its maximum exceeds one hundred

labelIndices.description: an empty series has no labels
twelve buckets or fewer are all labelled
past twelve the labels are thinned to about eight
the Float step differs from Double here: index 30 survives
and here Double would keep 60, Float does not
one more, where the two disagree again
screen: thirteen buckets get six labels
screen: a month of daily buckets
screen: the length whose Float step differs from Double for the report

barHeight.description: no value at all draws no bar
a dry bucket draws no bar
a tiny but non-zero value keeps a visible sliver
the sliver floor does not lift an ordinary bar
a value at the ceiling fills the plot
a zero ceiling cannot divide, and the floor still applies

donut.description: three slices fill the ring clockwise from twelve o'clock
a single category fills the whole ring

abbreviateWeekday.description: ASCII shorter than the cut is returned whole
A two-letter Latin abbreviation is unchanged
A longer Latin abbreviation is cut to two
A precomposed accent counts as one unit
A combining accent counts as two units, unlike a grapheme cut
A single CJK ideograph is returned whole
A Hangul syllable is returned whole
A Greek abbreviation is cut after two letters
A Cyrillic two-letter abbreviation is unchanged
A surrogate pair is one symbol of two units and survives the cut

ceiling.description: trend: the tallest bar decides when it exceeds the limit
trend: the limit line decides when nothing exceeds it
trend: an empty chart still leaves room for the limit line
bar chart: the tallest bar plus room for its printed value
bar chart: no bars, no ceiling
